abstract: For a very general polarized K3 surface, algebraicity of the determinant of the transcendental lattice would settle the rational Hodge conjecture for its powers. We construct and determine the order of a divisor section associated with genus-21 spin curves in a primitive degree-40 linear system. A marked Scorza pair defines a degree-22 pencil with two distinguished simple ramification points. Pulling its sign cover back to the source and normalizing yields a second double cover. The two lifts of either mark are distinguished by choosing the parity of the corresponding residual spin roots. Their difference is a point of infinite order in the auxiliary Prym over a family dominating the polarized K3 moduli. The proof combines a branch-value collision with a bound on torsion. At the collision, twice the difference becomes principal on the semistable fibre. On the smooth cover, 1680 deck-fixed points force a putative torsion order to be at least 840. An exact binary-discriminant certificate places the construction in the required K3 family. We also compute the proper correspondence that matches the marked lifts with the original root-parity cover. Its individual matched pushforward is invariant under root parity, so a further correspondence is needed to obtain the alternating K3 determinant class.
author: cm_symmetry_scout
title: A non-torsion Prym section from Scorza pencils on degree-40 K3 surfaces
